text.insert: Score integration gate, global regression protection, and PR handoff boundary.

The worker loop can create evidence and candidate patches, but the run baseline
changes only through the score integration gate. This keeps verified progress
separate from exploratory attempts.
Sessions And The Local Change Ledger

A run session is one grouping of changes measured against one frozen baseline.
Shipping moves a subset of that grouping upstream. A sync request only requests or
acquires dispatch authority; cancelling it leaves the current session and baseline
untouched. The local change ledger — carry-forward patches, facts, lessons, and
rejected hypotheses — persists across sessions: only shipped PR candidates ever
leave the system.

Because the orchestrator works alongside other contributors in an open-source
upstream, the sync boundary is a hard lock, not advice. Sync and merged-PR
intake are rejected while a run is active, because pulling upstream would
invalidate the baseline all worker evidence is measured against. Requesting sync
does not close the current session, and cancellation leaves that session unchanged.

A candidate should pass through these checks before it affects the board
baseline:
The runner has a selected checkpoint from the worker's target claim and write

An exact target score counts as exact only when the checkpoint also passed

hard gates. A 100% score with failed hard gates remains repair evidence and

The worker post-return repair gate is clean: no unaccepted write-set diff is
retained, configured runner-owned post-return checks passed, and any
loop has resolved rather than exhausted.
Local validation is preserved and unresolved local regressions are not kept.
The source remains reviewable and understandable.
The branch-level build/report refresh confirms the score movement.
The integration record captures the old and new progress signal.

After integration, the board can publish new facts and metrics. Active workers
do not need to be canceled just because the board changed; future target
packets can use the updated evidence.

The run should summarize accepted improvements, facts, rejected hypotheses,
stalls, score movement, validation transcripts, and review risks. That summary
is the bridge from autonomous work to human review.

Preship review, QA repair, and CI/local validation execute only inside an operator-entered campaign activation that holds the dispatch lease; the activation posts deduped comments for unresolved findings before the PR is ready for human review.

Disposition is consistent with the promotion policy: symbols blocked by the
gate become

and are readmitted at repair priority; a slice ships
without them or not at all. MATCHES-only shipping is unchanged — the gate

Adversarial cleanup and QA repair are allowed to lower fuzzy score or lose an
exact match when they remove overzealous worker output or maintainer-rejected
source shape. The lower-score result is reported and carried forward or routed
through an explicit improvement lane; the banned tactic is not restored simply
to preserve a score.

The QA repair lane extends this disposition before split planning: a
candidate-file sweep converts deterministic QA findings and file-backed review
findings into a repair queue, a resolver-style agent attempts source-level
repairs before minimal reverts, and each finding receives an explicit
disposition. Strict automated handoff treats warnings as repair targets:
worker L1 and

L2 both require zero QA findings, and draft
PR QA keeps the same strict default unless an operator explicitly selects
advisory warnings. Each repair queue item carries an authorized_write_set. The
repair lane retains authorized cross-file fixes, partially reverts only
unauthorized hunks, and returns blocked_needs_cross_file when the clean repair
requires a path outside that set; it does not restore the target source
wholesale. Clean-lower-score files stay out of ready status unless an operator
explicitly accepts that outcome. The ship-filter artifact feeds split planning
so queued, blocked, false-positive, or clean-lower-score files are not silently
included in match PRs.

The orchestrator does not create one PR per file, worker, symbol, or claim, and
it does not publish GitHub PRs automatically. Human-facing PR packaging is a
separate step after the run produces a coherent improvement bundle.

For review-sized handoff, the packaging step asks the orchestrator for a split
plan.

owns deterministic evidence collection: it inspects the
branch/worktree against the selected base ref, applies checkpoint lanes and
ship-filter verdicts, keeps every changed file assigned exactly once, and emits
suggested slice branches, titles, pathspecs, and patch commands. The default
strategy groups by Melee subsystem directories such as

. A declared cross-subsystem support file is assigned to the
match slice that motivates it and remains in that slice's manifest through
patch construction and isolation. Unassigned shared work remains a separate
slice so unrelated cross-cutting changes can be reviewed or stacked intentionally.

When a project or command selects the agent strategy, the PR splitter agent
receives the deterministic plan as evidence and proposes a smarter review
series: regrouped slices, order, titles, dependency notes, review focus, and PR
body summaries. The runner validates the proposal before using it. The agent
cannot add or drop files, change match/local lanes, mix lanes in one slice,
exceed the configured max-file ceiling, or decide that a file ships. Invalid
splitter output falls back to the deterministic plan with a warning.

. A slice becomes truly independent only after its complete manifest,

The PR splitter shapes the handoff series before remote PRs exist; one durable PR campaign then owns every series from that stable-point split through the review cycle, while the PR indexer analyzes merged PRs for reusable knowledge. A project permits at most one open campaign. Branch presentation, operator-gated batch publication, reviewer coordination, and operator-confirmed campaign closure stay outside the worker claim loop. Each series records its branch, upstream PR number, remote review status, feedback work items, and latest validation per
. Legacy split-PR records can be adopted into the campaign as durable series.

Background remote observation advances a published series through changes requested, approval, merge, or closure without acquiring the dispatch lease, and it ingests review feedback immediately as pending work items. The durable campaign remains mostly dormant while it waits for reviewers. Fixers and
validation run only inside an operator-entered activation that holds the dispatch lease; acquisition and release each record a
session-timeline entry. Fixes stay tied to the existing remote series and review thread.

THE PR GATE. The match-lane diff (worktree vs the base SHA, so uncommitted work counts) is applied onto the cached baseline worktree, rebuilt incrementally, and regression-checked there, then linted with upstream CI's check-issues container (clang semantic issues like -Wself-assign permuter slop or conflicting prototypes that the MWCC match build never reports). Files with lint issues drop to rework through the same survivor loop as regressions. pr_ready means: exactly what the PRs will contain produces new matches, zero regressions against the production baseline, and zero CI lint issues, regardless of how messy the local branch is. The worktree is reset afterwards so the per-SHA cache stays valid.
reconcile & re-verify
only when the ship set is blocked: the reconcile agent (`reconcile --mode ship-validate`) gets one fix loop, then the ship set re-verifies. Prepare fails only if regressions persist after that.
replan PR slices

when the survivor loop dropped files, the split plan regenerates against the verified verdict (`pr-split-plan --ship-status`): match slices keep only files that survived ship-set verification, and dropped files ride the local lane with their drop reasons. The plan the operator ships from never needs manual subtraction.
sync PR records
the PR board seeds from the final plan (state/pr_handoff/pr_records.json), so stage 4 lists exactly what to open.
save point

a hard `ship` save point anchors the session and the campaign source. The operator opens one durable campaign from that stable point; the campaign persists through review, with feedback ingested while dormant and fixes reserved for operator-entered activations.
